target_customer: Turkish shippers who need trucks, and the small fleets and independent truckers who supply them
problem: Freight forwarding in Turkey runs on phone calls, emails and face to face deals, and SME fleets hold about 95 percent of a fragmented trucking market.
business_model: Freight marketplace and brokerage with a margin on loads (FTL contract and spot)

founders.name: Berkay Adlim
education: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, BS Industrial Engineering
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked in logistics, procurement and warehousing from an early age and published research at Columbia; employers not named.

competitors.name: Yolda
competitors.what: Turkish digital freight forwarder and logistics startup
competitors.funding_then: 830,000 USD pre-seed in May 2020 and a further 1.9M USD reported by June 2021

competitors.name: TIRPORT
competitors.what: Istanbul based digital freight marketplace and brokerage
competitors.traction_then: Described by FreightWaves as building Turkey's largest digital freight marketplace

technical_complexity.rationale: A matching marketplace and mobile apps are standard engineering; the hard part was operations and trust with fragmented drivers.

defensibility.rationale: Two sided liquidity of loads and drivers helps, but rival load boards existed and drivers multi-home.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copycat by an incumbent was found in the sources opened.

market_need_then: YC launch post cites about 850,000 independent truckers and a 73 billion USD Turkish logistics market run on phone and email brokering.

identity.voice_and_tone: Upbeat, promotional and simple, with Turkish copy mixing logistics English terms such as FTL and Spot.

branding.brand_signature: Uber for trucks positioning in Turkish; slogan about tens of thousands of loads every day

brand_strength.rationale: Clear and local, with a name close to the Turkish word for truck (not confirmed by any source), but no evidence of brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Kamion built a trucking marketplace in a market of fragmented small fleets, joined YC in Summer 2022 and closed a reported 2 million dollar seed in December 2022. Its site now claims over 50,000 drivers and more than 10,000 loads shared daily, and a 2023 article reports about 10 million dollars of revenue. It remains active with no shutdown or acquisition found, so its outcome so far is steady growth.
notes: Seed of 2M USD is stated by a university news item and, per the search result, a CB Insights news item dated 2022-12-14; CB Insights lists YC as lead which is unusual and is recorded as stated. Seedtable lists a 500K USD pre-seed in June 2022 (aggregator only, unverified). Aggregator totals of 2.5M USD and a PitchBook entry dated 2025-08 without amount are unverified. Founding year conflicts: PitchBook 2020, CB Insights 2021. Revenue figure of 10M USD for 2023 comes from a single news aggregator page and is unverified. TIRPORT source is undated in what was seen. Yolda funding sources are Tech.eu and TurkeyMonitor via search results. No outcome events found.
